surveyAnswers.q2: I would say one of the main challenges was knowing that a robot's actions might technically make sense, even if it didn't make sense in a larger context. For example, it made sense that a robot might wait around to grab parts as it allowed the other robot to finish the job and for the robots to team up in sync again and quickly fill a machine, but it didn't make sense in the larger context because they didn't use the second machine - which would have enabled them to keep working constantly. Or, it made sense having the grey robot only focus on boxes - technically, but in practice it was clunky and unhelping for the needed teamwork and the robot made mistakes. Sometimes it was also hard to process what all four robots were doing and decide what action seemed most/least important.
surveyAnswers.q3: Perhaps differently colored boxes around them or a breakdown of the basic reasoning/instructions they were given to see if they were correctly following those instructions.
surveyAnswers.q1: I would generally focus on one robot at a time, so that I could fully pay attention to what it was doing and what it's main trajectory seemed to be - or its goals. I would then look at the process between the robots and see if they were maximizing how they work together or help one another in order to quickly accomplish the task and drop off boxes.

surveyAnswers.q1: I watched each episode as a whole and then focused on each robots behavior from beginning to end by replaying the episodes and segments to determine their behavior.  I noted how they did or didn't work together, movement issues,  and whether they were "focused" on the task they were trying to complete.  For example, after picking a part up did they go directly to the machine, or did they move around randomly before going to the machine.
surveyAnswers.q3: The video controls (especially in notating problems) were kind of "clunky" to use and it was hard to be precise in their use.  The video as well wasn't very fluid in looking at movements.  At one point with two robots blocking each other and not moving, going frame by frame it went from them blocking each other, to one robot being several movements away despite it being the next frame.  It would also be nice to be able to highlight individual robots so that you can more easily focus on their interactions, as trying to focus on one or two robots you would often have a random robot break your attention.
surveyAnswers.q2: Having more than two definitely posed more of a challenge of tracking each separate robot's behavior, but having more also made it easier to determine how well they were or weren't working together.  Also overall it seems that across all of the robots in each scenario their actions could be kind of chaotic and lacking direction, especially without a baseline to determine how the robots should behave.
